idea.title: 3 snack vending machines in US offices and gyms

source.text: Buying 3 snack vending machines and placing them in offices and gyms. Launch country US, budget $10,000, 8 hours a week, goal side income, no special edge. Just go: do not ask questions. Use the slug vending-machines.

idea.problem: Office workers and gym members want a quick snack on site.
idea.customer: Location hosts: office managers and gym owners in the US who would let an operator place a snack machine (end buyers: their staff and members)
idea.solution: Buy 3 snack vending machines and place them in offices and gyms.
assumptions: Used/refurbished snack machines (~USD 1,900 each) with a Nayax card reader, because new machines were not priced and the budget is USD 10,000.
Average vend ticket USD 2.01 (Cantaloupe 2026) and cost of goods ~50% of revenue (The Hustle operator survey).
Location commission 10% of gross; base gross USD 250 per machine per month (below the survivor-biased survey average of USD 309).
No location is secured yet; the founder pitches sites by walk-in and phone.
Founder time valued at USD 25/hour for CAC.
Headless run: no intake questions asked (user said just go).

answers.question: Is any location already secured?
answers.effect: Headless run: assumed no location secured; channel_readiness 2.

verdict.launch_reason: The founder is US-based and set the US as the only market.

gross_margin.note: COGS ~50% + 10% commission + card fees leave ~36% per vend on a $2.01 ticket (estimate); R5 costs_eat_margin.

ltv_cac.note: LTV ~$2,822 vs ~$2,455 per placed machine (capex + pitching): 1.15 (estimate).

pricing_power.note: Average vend ticket $2.01 anchors price; hosts negotiate 10-25% commission; free office snacks cap it.

build_effort.note: Buying used machines takes days; landing 3 sites takes weeks (10:1 to 100+ pitches per yes).

skills_match.note: Needs cold sales, restocking and basic repairs: learnable, no special skill.

capital_needed.note: 3 refurbished machines + readers + stock ~$7,600-8,000: fits the $10k budget with thin margin for repairs.

time_to_mvp.note: First vend in ~4-6 weeks: site hunt, purchase, move, card-reader activation (estimate).

sales_cycle.note: Office manager or gym owner decides in 1-4 weeks; some sites are locked by an incumbent operator contract.

channel_readiness.note: No site secured; best sites 'already saturated with machines'; some operators make 100+ calls per site.

search_demand.note: Daily mass-market need; 81M US gym members (HFA 2025), but offices at ~56% of pre-2020 occupancy.

trend.note: Industry $40.04B (+18.3%) but growth is smart coolers; IBISWorld sees operators declining over 5 years.

willingness_to_pay.note: People pay ~$2 per vend, 78% cashless; 32% of employers give snacks free (SHRM 2018).

free_alternatives.note: Free employer snacks (32% of employers, 2018) and catered lunches cover part of the job.

competitor_density.note: Operators over $10M take 65.2% of sales; micro-markets and a side-hustle crowd fight for the rest.

differentiation.note: Same machines, same snacks, same commission pitch as every other new operator; no edge stated.

legal_regulatory.note: Mostly sales-tax registration and local licences ($0-500); FDA labelling only from 20 machines.

platform_dependency.note: Each host can remove the machine at will; a big operator offering a smart cooler can take the site.

market_risk.note: Durable need, but hybrid work and GLP-1 users cutting savory snacks ~10% squeeze volume.

skills.note: No vending or B2B sales track record stated.

assets.note: No locations, network or audience: the asset that matters in vending ('location rights') is missing.

interest.note: Goal stated as side income only.

sam.reasoning: $40.04B industry (VMW 2026) x 0.33 snack share x 0.124 office share of locations = ~$1.6B; gyms not split out

competitors_found.reasoning: Named in research: Canteen, Five Star, Avanti, 365 Retail Markets, SnackNation, free employer snacks, turnkey route sellers, local side-hustle operators

demand_trend.value: flat to falling for classic snack machines; rising for smart coolers

variable_cost_per_unit.reasoning: COGS 50% x 2.01 = 1.00 + commission 10% = 0.20 + card fee 5.95% x 78% cashless = 0.09

expected_lifetime.reasoning: Assumed 3-year placement life of a refurbished machine at one host; no sourced location churn found

conversion_rate_pct.reasoning: Guides cite 5-10 approaches per yes and 20-30 pitches for 2-3 yeses (~10%); The Hustle reports 100+ calls for some

cac.reasoning: Machine 1,900 + Nayax reader 399 + activation 30 + 5 h pitching x $25 = 125 (capex counted because each site needs its own machine)

ltv.reasoning: (250 gross - 125 COGS - 25 commission - 11.6 card % - 9.99 reader fee) = 78.4/month x 36 months

payback_months.reasoning: CAC 2,455 / 78.4 monthly contribution per machine; ~39 months for the whole $7,800 setup after insurance

fixed_costs_month.reasoning: General liability $37 (Insureon median) + 3 Nayax monthly fees x $9.99

break_even_customers_per_month.reasoning: (capex 7,600 / 24 months + fixed 67) / 0.72 contribution per vend = ~533 vends (~178 per machine, ~8 per business day)

time_to_first_revenue_weeks.reasoning: 2-3 weeks of walk-ins for 3 sites at 8 h/week + 1-2 weeks to buy, move and activate machines

rules_applied.effect: Profit potential 2.0 (36% margin, LTV:CAC 1.15): total 52 - 10 = 42, NO-GO

type_checks.note: At ~56% office occupancy and ~1 vend per employee per week, an office needs ~90-100 badged staff to reach $50/week; small offices and gyms fall short.
Permits are cheap (state sales-tax permit $0-50, local licences $50-500); capex ~$7,600-8,000 fits the $10k budget, though payback is ~31-39 months.

confidence.note: Per-machine sales for offices vs gyms are not split; real quotes from 30 local sites would raise it.

verdict.cheapest_test: Pitch 30 sites with 100+ on-site staff in 7 days before buying anything; need 2+ written yeses.
kill_criteria: Fewer than 2 written placement yeses from 30 pitches by day 7 -> do not buy machines
Signed sites with fewer than 100 on-site staff per shift -> do not place there
Modelled payback above 24 months at the signed sites by day 7 -> stop

rescue.change: Pitch first, buy later: sign 3 blue-collar or 24/7 sites (warehouses, plants, hospitals) with 100+ on-site staff before buying used machines.
rescue.why: Fixes location_traffic and channel_readiness; ~$400/machine/month lifts LTV:CAC to ~2 and clears R7.
rescue.cost: $0 until a site signs, then ~$2,330 per machine

rescue.change: Buy a small existing route with verified card-reader sales history instead of starting cold.
rescue.why: Removes the placement hunt and proves revenue before paying; fixes channel_readiness and time_to_mvp.
rescue.requires: 4x the budget or seller financing; diligence on telemetry data

narrative.answer: NO-GO. Three snack machines at sites you still have to find net about **$200/month** on ~$7,800 of capex: a **31-39 month payback** before repairs, at roughly $6 an hour for your 8 hours a week.
tldr: After **50% cost of goods**, a 10% host commission and card fees, each $2.01 vend keeps ~36%: the margin cannot carry the machines.
The best sites are taken: operators over $10M hold **65.2%** of sales and smart coolers are displacing machines in key locations.
The only fix is to sign high-traffic sites (100+ on-site staff) **before** buying anything.
narrative.lesson: In vending the machine is cheap and the location is the business: no secured site, no business.

key_findings.title: Unit economics: ~$200/month for three machines
key_findings.detail: At **$250** gross per machine, COGS ~50%, 10% commission and card fees leave ~$78 per machine per month; payback **~31 months** (estimate from The Hustle survey).

key_findings.title: Big operators and smart coolers own the sites
key_findings.detail: Operators over $10M take **65.2%** of sales; smart coolers are **displacing** machines in key locations (Vending Market Watch, 2025).

key_findings.title: Offices are half empty
key_findings.detail: Kastle's 10-city occupancy sat at **56.5%** in late October 2026, so a 100-person office feeds a machine like a **56-person** one.

narrative.recommendation: Do not buy machines. Spend 7 days pitching 30 sites with 100+ on-site staff; buy only if 2+ sign a placement letter.
narrative.steelman: Cashless is now **78%** of vending sales and the industry grew to $40.04B in 2025, so a disciplined operator with 3 high-traffic sites can earn a semi-passive few hundred dollars a month. The evidence says this holds only for sites with **100+** on-site staff, which incumbents already serve.

premortem.cause: Only leftover small sites say yes; machines gross ~$150/month and net under $40 each.
premortem.early_signal: Fewer than 75 vends per machine in the first 30 days (card-reader dashboard).

premortem.cause: Can't sign 3 sites in time; machines sit in a garage while the budget is spent.
premortem.early_signal: Fewer than 2 yeses from 30 pitches in the first 2 weeks.

premortem.cause: A host swaps the machine for a big operator's smart cooler or micro-market.
premortem.early_signal: Host mentions an existing operator contract or a cooler offer during the first month.

changes.what: Smart coolers reached 33.5% of deployed equipment, nearly matching glass-front machines.
Cashless reached 78% of vending sales in 2025, with an average ticket of $2.01.
Office occupancy peaked at a post-2020 record in December 2025 and stalled near 56% in fall 2026.
GLP-1 user households cut savory snack spending about 10% (Cornell/Numerator).
TikTok and YouTube vending side-hustle videos pulled in a wave of new operators.

why_now.note: Cashless is no longer an edge, coolers are taking the best sites and a side-hustle crowd chases the rest: the window for classic snack machines is closing.

icp.who: Facilities or office manager, or owner, of a US site with 100+ on-site staff per shift and no current machine (warehouse, plant, hospital, 24/7 gym).
where: Walk-ins at industrial parks and plants
Gym owner groups and front desks
icp.pays_for_today: Nothing: operators pay hosts a 10-25% commission; some offices buy snack delivery (SnackNation from $199).
icp.budget: USD 0: hosts expect free install, free service and a commission.
icp.trigger: The current machine is empty or broken, the incumbent operator leaves, a new site opens, or staff ask for food on night shifts.

customer.segment: Office managers and gym owners who host machines; end buyers are their staff and members.
customer.pain: Staff want a quick snack on site without leaving the building.
customer.today: Incumbent full-line operators, micro-markets, smart coolers, free employer snacks or a nearby convenience store.

use_cases.name: Gym lobby
use_cases.who_pays: Members, mostly drinks and protein bars

use_cases.name: Warehouse or plant with shifts (100+ staff)
use_cases.who_pays: Shift workers, $2-5 per worker per week
use_cases.effort: Hard to win, but the only profile that clears payback

free_alternative.evidence: 32% of employers offered free snacks and drinks in 2018 (SHRM), covering part of the job, not all of it; searched free office snacks and catering.

strong_competitor.evidence: Operators above $10M revenue are 10% of operators but take 65.2% of sales (Vending Market Watch, 2025); Canteen runs 225+ distribution locations.

graveyard.evidence: Bodega/Stockwell shut down on 2020-07-01 despite $45M raised; FTC cases (1997-2007) show vending 'location' sellers whose buyers never recovered their investment.

no_distribution.evidence: A channel exists but is costly: cold walk-ins at ~10 pitches per yes, some operators make 100+ calls; first-year value per site (~$940) still exceeds pitching cost.

costs_eat_margin.evidence: About 50% of revenue goes to product, 10-25% to the host and ~5-6% to card fees (The Hustle, 2024): ~36% gross margin, under the 50% bar.

weak_demand.evidence: Overall convenience services grew to $31.1B in 2025 (NAMA); growth is in coolers and micro-markets, and IBISWorld sees operators declining, so the classic format is flat, not collapsing.

legal_platform_risk.evidence: Sales-tax registration and local licences ($0-500) are the main rules; FDA calorie labelling applies only from 20 machines.

saturated_wave.evidence: A side-hustle wave exists (VendingNation Facebook group 6k to 14.5k members in H1 2024), but no count of new entrants in the last 12 months was found, so the rule is not applied.

competitors.name: Canteen (Compass Group)
competitors.gap: Ignores sites too small for a full-line route

competitors.name: Smart coolers and micro-markets (365 Retail Markets, Avanti)
competitors.gap: Needs larger sites and fresh-food logistics

competitors.name: SnackNation office snack delivery
competitors.gap: Employer pays; no per-snack revenue for an operator

competitors.name: Free employer snacks and catering
competitors.gap: Absent at most gyms and blue-collar sites

competitors.name: Turnkey route sellers and locators
competitors.traction_note: Template listings in 5+ cities on BizBuySell
competitors.gap: Sell the same placement play to every new operator

competitors.name: Local side-hustle operators
competitors.gap: Same pitch, same machines: no edge either

scenarios.name: Pessimistic
scenarios.note: $150/machine leftover sites, 15% commission: ~$70/month net, never pays back the machines.

risks.risk: Repairs: bill validators, spirals and card readers fail; one owner reported ~$3,000 of repairs in 14 months.
risks.mitigation: Buy refurbished with a 90-day warranty and keep $1,500 in reserve.

risks.risk: Locator or turnkey scams promising 'prime locations'.
risks.mitigation: Demand the FTC one-page disclosure 7 days before paying; never pay for a 'guaranteed' site.

risks.risk: Host removes the machine for a big operator's cooler.
risks.mitigation: Sign a 12-month placement agreement with 30-day notice.

risks.risk: State vending sales tax: e.g. Texas taxes vended snacks and candy that are exempt in stores.
risks.mitigation: Register for sales tax and price tax-inclusive.

test_plan.step: List 40 sites within 20 minutes with 100+ on-site staff per shift: warehouses, plants, hospitals, 24/7 gyms.
test_plan.verify: 40 sites listed with a name and estimated headcount

test_plan.step: Walk in or call 30 of them; offer free install, free service and a 10% commission.
test_plan.verify: 30 pitches logged; at least 3 verbal yeses

test_plan.step: Ask each yes for headcount per shift, current operator and a signed one-page placement letter.
test_plan.verify: At least 2 signed letters at 100+ staff sites

test_plan.step: Price 3 refurbished machines and Nayax readers; model payback at $250 and $400 per machine.
test_plan.verify: Modelled payback under 24 months, or stop

rescue.change: Pitch first, buy later: sign 3 blue-collar or 24/7 sites (warehouses, plants, hospitals) with 100+ on-site staff before buying used machines.
rescue.why: Fixes location_traffic and channel_readiness; ~$400/machine/month lifts LTV:CAC to ~2 and clears R7.
rescue.cost: $0 until a site signs, then ~$2,330 per machine

rescue.change: Buy a small existing route with verified card-reader sales history instead of starting cold.
rescue.why: Removes the placement hunt and proves revenue before paying; fixes channel_readiness and time_to_mvp.
rescue.requires: 4x the budget or seller financing; diligence on telemetry data
